messages:
maria (sec-eng): Heads-up: customer BYOK asks for ephemeral wrapping keys on import into our HSMs. We need a short RFC on custody boundaries, RBAC changes, and how audit logs prove chain-of-custody for compliance (SOC2/FIPS).
kevin (platform): +1. Do we treat ephemeral wrap keys as customer-owned material or transient host material? affects access reviewers and keystore RBAC.
olivia (prod-sre): my instinct: ephemeral wrap keys are customer material while present; ops must not have unwrap perms. We can allow a managed rewrap path for failures but it must be heavily audited and gated.
rahul (kms-plumbing): implementation note: we can import using an offline-import key loaded on HSM, then immediately wrap customer CMK with ephemeral master and zeroize local copy. Policy can emit audit events. Example log line we can use in evidence: ```[2024-09-12T22:14:03Z] actor=import-service action=import_key key_id=cmk-0xabc wrap_key=ephemeral-20240912 host=hsm-amber outcome=success request_id=req-9b2f```
maria (sec-eng): Perfect. Need explicit RBAC change list: who can request an import, who can approve rewrap, emergency revoke flows. Also retention for these audit logs — legal wants 3 years for some customers.
anne (legal): 3 years is typical for enterprise contracts. For PCI/FedRAMP customers it might be longer. Also need immutable, tamper-evident storage (S3 object lock / WORM or external log archive).
kevin (platform): Proposal: create two new roles: `byok-importer` (can initiate import, read import status), `byok-auditor` (read logs, request attestation). Only a small Ops roster gets `byok-importer`; cross-check with SRE oncall. Add automatic Slack approval workflow when importer triggers rewrap.
olivia (prod-sre): can we minimize blast radius for `byok-importer`? Maybe require MFA + hardware token + just-in-time approval window (30m). Also log an immutable snapshot to our sign-and-store system.
rahul (kms-plumbing): JIT approval is doable. We'll add an HSM-level policy that marks imported keys as `customer_sealed=true` and forbids `unwrap` unless `approved_by` header present and cached in HSM session. For audit we attach the approving principal and PCR digest.
maria (sec-eng): What about vuln triage if a firmware bug affects ephemeral wrap key handling? Customers will expect proof we rotated/contained.
kevin (platform): Runbook: (1) isolate affected HSM pool (traffic drain), (2) snapshot all import audit logs to external archive, (3) rotate ephemeral master keys and rewrap CMKs if attestable, (4) notify impacted customers + compliance, (5) provide forensic packet of logs + signed attestation.
olivia (prod-sre): Also add a telemetry alert: any `import_key` with `wrap_key` older than 12h should fire an ops alert — prevents stale ephemeral reuse.
rahul (kms-plumbing): From KMS integration side: provide `import_id` and signed `import_attestation` blob back to customer for their records. Support API: `POST /keys/{id}/import-status` returns `signed_attestation` and `log_slice`.
anne (legal): That API + signable attestation satisfies auditors usually. Ensure attestation includes HSM serial, firmware version, signing key id, and timestamp.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20240912-0042 (byok-import-audit-snapshot). Assigned: olivia, rahul.
maria (sec-eng): Action items: kevin to draft RBAC rule changes + JIT flow, rahul to spec import/attestation API, olivia to add alert and runbook steps, anne to confirm retention language. Please drop PRs and I'll consolidate into a short RFC by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
